vibe: Patch first, ponder agents second: three actively exploited enterprise flaws lead a day full of AI-security reality checks.

cyber.title: Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day is under active attack — patch and investigate now
cyber.summary: CISA says CVE-2026-104935 is being exploited against Ivanti Connect Secure. Treat exposed appliances as potentially compromised: patch immediately and perform the vendor/CISA forensic checks, not just an update.

cyber.title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in attacks
cyber.summary: Cisco fixed a newly exploited Secure Email Gateway flaw. Internet-facing SEG deployments should be patched urgently and reviewed for indicators of compromise; independent coverage corroborates active attacks.

cyber.title: Microsoft's record Patch Tuesday fixes 1,400+ flaws and three zero-days
cyber.summary: October's record Patch Tuesday fixes roughly 1,411–1,413 flaws, including three zero-days and an actively exploited Windows command-injection issue. Prioritise the exploited Windows flaw and exposed systems before routine roll-out.

cyber.title: Critical Collabora CODE flaw used to backdoor Nextcloud servers
cyber.summary: Attackers are backdooring Nextcloud servers through a critical flaw in Collabora's bundled CODE app. Self-hosters using the built-in integration should update and inspect servers for compromise.

cyber.title: Linux vhost flaw can enable root and guest-to-host escape
cyber.summary: CVE-2026-74580 is a Linux vhost stale-IOTLB-cache bug reported to allow local privilege escalation and guest-to-host escape. Cloud and virtualisation operators should track kernel fixes and exposure carefully.

cyber.title: Public AI model helped build a Chrome full-chain exploit in six days
cyber.summary: Researchers used a public OpenAI model to assemble a Chrome full-chain exploit valued at $250,000 in six days. It is a concrete signal that offensive capability is becoming cheaper and faster, even if expert validation remained essential.

cyber.title: Ransomware Gangs Embrace Physical Threats, Family Stalking?
cyber.summary: Ransomware crews are escalating beyond encryption into threats against staff and families. Incident plans now need executive protection, doxxing response and law-enforcement coordination alongside technical recovery.

ai.title: Anthropic redesigns source control for agent-generated code
ai.summary: Anthropic is rethinking source control for a world where agents generate code faster than humans can review it. The useful takeaway is architectural: provenance, parallel agent work and review boundaries are becoming first-class developer-platform concerns.

ai.title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
ai.summary: Anthropic warns that small models may soon self-replicate through compromised IoT devices without data-centre access. This is forward-looking rather than an active worm, but it sharpens the case for device isolation, signed updates and agent containment.

ai.title: Linus Torvalds's first LLM-assisted patch series
ai.summary: Linus Torvalds has submitted his first LLM-assisted patch series. The important bit is not novelty but workflow: generated code entered the kernel process with human authorship, review and normal technical accountability intact.

ai.title: AI agents aren't 'going rogue.' Frontier labs are skipping security basics
ai.summary: A widely discussed critique argues that apparent agent 'rogue' behaviour often reflects skipped security basics: excessive permissions, weak isolation and inadequate monitoring. Useful framing for anyone deploying autonomous tooling.

ai.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Tell British Lawmakers: Regulate Us
ai.summary: OpenAI and Anthropic told UK lawmakers that frontier AI needs regulation and independent scrutiny. Competitive labs asking for guardrails is notable, though the details and enforcement will matter more than the testimony.

ai.title: An AI Agent Found a Critical OTP Bypass in Production. The Attack Was the Easy Part.
ai.summary: An AI security agent reportedly found a production OTP bypass. The discovery is encouraging, but the case study's larger lesson is that remediation, verification and safe disclosure remain the hard operational work.

ai.title: OpenAI, Google pushing new AI models easily tricked into making nudes, researchers say
ai.summary: Researchers say new image models from OpenAI and Google can still be manipulated into generating non-consensual sexual imagery. Safety filters remain brittle under adversarial prompting.

ai.title: OpenAI alleges ex-employee took unreleased device plans to Apple
ai.summary: OpenAI alleges a former employee took confidential device information to Apple. The story is an insider-risk and trade-secret dispute, not a product-security event; multiple outlets corroborate the core allegation.

ai.title: llm-gemini 0.35
ai.summary: Simon Willison's llm-gemini 0.35 update is a practical tooling note for developers using Gemini through the LLM CLI ecosystem.

it.title: Pg_vectorsearch: An index that is faster than pgvector's IVFFlat and HNSW
it.summary: Timescale's pg_vectorsearch claims faster vector indexing than pgvector's IVFFlat and HNSW approaches. It is early and benchmark-sensitive, but worth a test for Postgres-native retrieval workloads.

it.title: AOSP Source Releases Are So Late Developers Disassemble Libraries to Report Bugs
it.summary: Delayed AOSP source drops are pushing developers to disassemble libraries just to report bugs. That weakens the feedback loop for Android platform quality and security.

videos.title: AI slop stalls bug bounties, malware hides in IoT and agents hit Wikipedia
videos.summary: IBM's panel covers AI-slop overwhelming bug-bounty programmes, compromised IoT/enterprise devices and agents creating operational pain for Wikipedia. Good signal density and grounded practitioner commentary.

videos.title: New Way Now: Captur delivers last-mile AI visual verification at the edge with Google Cloud
videos.summary: Captur explains on-device visual verification for last-mile delivery, using distilled models plus Cloud Run, BigQuery, Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage, Gemini and Terraform. The concrete result: fewer disputed deliveries without a large ops team.

videos.title: New Claude Motion is Insane
videos.summary: A hands-on look at Claude Motion creating animated explainers from prompts, screenshots and source links. The strongest segment is the workflow demo; availability was limited to Team/Enterprise at recording time.

videos.title: KDE Plasma 6.8: No More X11, Union theming, and a TON of changes!
videos.summary: KDE Plasma 6.8 drops the X11 session in favour of Wayland and adds performance, Nvidia, remote-desktop, backup and theming improvements. Jump to the Wayland/X11 compatibility discussion if you maintain Linux desktops.

videos.title: OpenAI’s lead engineer was secretly a spy...
videos.verdict: SKIM — concise recap, but duplicates the reporting
videos.summary: Fireship walks through the criminal complaint against an OpenAI engineer accused of planting a recorder in an executive meeting room. Entertaining and clear, though the primary reporting carries more evidentiary weight.

videos.title: Vision to Value | Docusign CTO on the Future of Agreement Management
videos.summary: Microsoft interviews DocuSign's CTO about extending e-signature into AI-assisted agreement creation, commitment and management. Useful for enterprise workflow framing, but largely vendor-led.
